clue.text: Kept excavating capital of Greece for sea creature

parts.note: to keep digging is to dig on, so 'kept excavating' gives DUG ON

indicators.note: the capital of a word is its first letter, so only the opening letter of Greece is used

explanation.surface: An archaeologist digs on in Greece and turns up a marine animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital of Greece' looks like Athens but is just the letter G, added after DUG ON.
explanation.definitionFit: The dugong is a large plant-eating marine mammal, a relative of the manatee.

clue.text: Member of political party is upset over soldier hissing

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so these letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: LIB is short for a Liberal, a member of that party
taken as written
a soldier ant is a kind of ant, so soldier gives ANT

explanation.surface: A party member is annoyed by a soldier who keeps hissing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns LIB IS into SIBIL; 'over' puts it above ANT in the down light.
explanation.definitionFit: Sibilant describes a sound made with a hiss, such as s or sh.

clue.text: Curse, standing under wide sign in part of department store

indicators.note: in a down clue, standing under means placed below the other pieces

parts.note: W is the cricket abbreviation for a wide
an omen is a sign of things to come
to curse is to swear

explanation.surface: A shopper swears beneath a big sign in a department store.
explanation.walkthrough: 'standing under' puts SWEAR below W and OMEN in the down light. A wide is an extra in cricket, a ball bowled out of the batter's reach.
explanation.definitionFit: Womenswear is the clothing section for women, one department within a large store.

clue.text: After demolition, one's left with broken house

indicators.note: demolition knocks something to bits, so the letters that follow are rebuilt in a new order
something that has left has gone, so this letter is taken out of the word with

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A building has been knocked down, leaving only broken rubble behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' removes the I, and 'After demolition' rebuilds the rest. Knebworth House is a stately home in Hertfordshire, England, famous for its rock concerts.
explanation.definitionFit: Knebworth is an English country house, so 'house' names it by its type.

clue.text: Write articles about dismissing leader when finished

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, which is sent away here

parts.note: a journalist who writes articles about something is said to cover it

explanation.surface: A reporter writes up the sacking of a party leader once it is all over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dismissing leader' takes the C off COVER. 'leader' looks like a politician but is only the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: When a match or event is over, it has come to an end.

clue.text: Hispanic US city? Power in US city very much linked to Spain

parts.note: E is the international vehicle code for Spain (España)

indicators.note: the power letter sits inside the abbreviation for the US city

parts.note: LA is short for Los Angeles
P is the physics symbol for power
so, as in 'I love it so', means very much

explanation.surface: Electricity in Los Angeles is closely tied to Spanish interests.
explanation.walkthrough: 'linked to Spain' joins E on the front of LPA and SO. The question mark flags that the name is Spanish, meaning 'the pass'.
explanation.definitionFit: El Paso is a Texas city on the Mexican border with a Spanish name and a largely Hispanic population.

clue.text: Way of working with group after blight does for monkey

indicators.note: the way of working and group come after the blight word, which therefore goes first

parts.note: to blight something is to mar it
MO is short for modus operandi, a way of working
a set is a group

explanation.surface: A new working method with a team fixes a crop blight for a monkey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' reverses the clue's order of pieces; 'does for' is only a link meaning 'gives'.
explanation.definitionFit: A marmoset is a small South American monkey.

clue.text: Something to follow tango, even

definitions.meaning: in the NATO phonetic alphabet, the word for U comes right after Tango for T
even, as an adjective, means the same all through, unvarying

explanation.surface: A dancer wonders what comes next after a tango, keeping steady.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tango' looks like the dance, but it is the radio code word for T.
explanation.definitionFit: Uniform as an adjective means unchanging and regular, the same as even.

clue.text: King avoiding observances for deity

indicators.note: avoiding means staying out, so the king letter is left out of the observances word

parts.note: to mark an occasion is to observe it, so marks are observances
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A monarch skips the religious rites meant for a god.
explanation.walkthrough: 'avoiding' drops K from MARKS.
explanation.definitionFit: Mars is the Roman god of war.

clue.text: Short story and French article trailing volume set during holiday period

indicators.note: the article trails, so it comes last
the volume letter is set within the holiday word

parts.note: Noel is Christmas, a holiday period
la is the French feminine word for 'the'

explanation.surface: A short tale and a French piece follow a book released over the Christmas break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set during' and 'trailing' build the word NOVEL plus a tail; the definition is fair because a novella is a short novel.
explanation.definitionFit: A novella is a work of fiction longer than a short story but shorter than a novel.

clue.text: US military gear? Nothing was run by sailor

parts.note: O, the round figure zero, stands for nothing
to have lived is to have been, so lived stands for was
R is the cricket abbreviation for run
AB, able-bodied seaman, is a common crossword sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor managed a show that came to nothing, in American army style.
explanation.definitionFit: Olive drab is the dull greenish colour of US Army uniforms and kit, so it can stand for that gear.

clue.text: Region is deficient in pragmatic behaviour

indicators.note: lacking these letters, so is is removed from the longer word

parts.note: realism is a practical, pragmatic attitude
taken as written

explanation.surface: An area is said to lack a practical approach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deficient in' takes IS out of REALISM; 'is' reads like the verb of the sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: A realm is a kingdom or domain, a region ruled or defined in some way.

clue.text: Drink and chat with son about origin of life

indicators.note: the chat and son letters go round the next letter

parts.note: gas is informal for idle chat

indicators.note: the origin of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Have a drink and talk with your son about how life began.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts L (from 'origin of life') inside GAS plus S.
explanation.definitionFit: A glass is a drink as served, as in 'a glass of wine'.

clue.text: Sinister: oxygen getting less, after suppression of oxygen

parts.note: O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

indicators.note: the second oxygen letter is pressed down inside the less word

parts.note: minus means less, as in five minus two
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: Something sinister is happening as oxygen runs short after being cut off.
explanation.walkthrough: O goes first; 'after suppression of' puts another O inside MINUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ominous threatens harm, which is a menacing, sinister quality.

clue.text: Ship's unwelcoming response meeting wave

parts.note: an icy, frosty response is unwelcoming, so it gives ice
a breaker is a large wave crashing on shore

explanation.surface: A ship gets a cold welcome as a big wave hits it.
explanation.definitionFit: An icebreaker is a ship built to cut a path through frozen seas.

clue.text: Equipment from the past brought in to crush endless flowers

indicators.note: the equipment phrase is brought inside the crushing word
without its end, so the final letter of the crush word goes

parts.note: to crush something is to mash it
a rig is a set of equipment
something from the past is old

explanation.surface: Old gear is used to flatten a bed of flowers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' drops the last letter, giving MAS, and 'brought in to' sets the equipment inside. 'crush' reads like the verb of the sentence but only supplies letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Marigolds are bright orange or yellow garden flowers.

clue.text: Having nowhere else to turn before we arrived here on tour?

definitions.meaning: the idiom means when all other options have failed

definitions.text: before we arrived here on tour?
definitions.meaning: read literally, the phrase means at the previous holiday town on the trip

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading takes 'resort' as a holiday town and 'last' as the one before, so 'in the last resort' is where a touring party stayed before this one.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a desperate final option, and literally names the previous holiday town on a tour.

clue.text: Privy to sealing off main areas when appropriate?

indicators.note: the privy phrase seals the other piece inside it, closing it off

parts.note: to be privy to a secret is to be in on it
the main is the sea, so areas of it are seas

explanation.surface: Someone in the know about closing off the sea at the right time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sealing off' signals enclosure. 'Privy' tempts as a toilet but means in on a secret; 'main' is the old poetic word for the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that is in season is available at the proper time of year, so the phrase means at the fitting time.

clue.text: Cruise company with this would be a joke

definitions.text: Cruise company with this would be a joke

parts.words: Cruise company with this would be a joke
parts.note: a cruise firm owning just a single ship would be laughable, and the phrase for that is also a short gag

explanation.walkthrough: A cruise line with only one ship would be absurd; the two words for its fleet also name a quick joke.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-liner is a joke told in a single sentence; split, it describes a fleet of one ship.

clue.text: Spoke without end about a strange retreating warrior

indicators.note: the trimmed spoke word goes round the other pieces
losing its end, so the final letter of the spoke word goes

parts.note: spoke, as a past tense, means said

indicators.note: going backwards, so these letters are read from right to left

parts.note: taken as written
rum is old British slang for strange

explanation.surface: Someone talks endlessly about an odd warrior who is falling back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without end' trims the last letter, 'retreating' turns A RUM into MURA, and 'about' wraps it. Rum meaning strange is old-fashioned British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: A samurai was a member of Japan's feudal military class, a warrior.

clue.text: Evil male supported by literary heroine

indicators.note: in a down clue, a piece supported by another sits above it

parts.note: Alice is the heroine of Lewis Carroll's Wonderland books

explanation.surface: A wicked man is propped up by a famous girl from fiction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supported by' puts M on top of ALICE in the down light.
explanation.definitionFit: Malice is the wish to do harm, an evil intent.

clue.text: Some woodwind identified in studies in sound

indicators.note: said out loud, so the word is spelt as it is heard rather than as written

parts.note: to read a subject is to study it, so studies gives reads

explanation.surface: Some wind instruments are named in research into acoustics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in sound' looks like part of a study of acoustics, but it signals that READS is replaced by a word pronounced the same way.
explanation.definitionFit: Reeds are instruments such as the oboe and clarinet, sounded through a vibrating reed.

clue.text: Fool brought in for one reason

indicators.note: the fool word is brought inside the other piece

parts.note: say, as in 'take a fruit, say an apple', means for one
a nit is a fool, short for nitwit

explanation.surface: An idiot is called in to explain one particular cause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought in' signals the container. 'reason' looks like a cause but means a sound mind, as in 'lose your reason'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sanity is soundness of mind, which is what 'reason' means in that phrase.

clue.text: Present judge is outspoken

indicators.note: spoken out loud, so the word is entered as it sounds, not as written

parts.note: a judge hears a case, so judge gives hear

explanation.surface: The current judge speaks his mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outspoken' looks like frank speech but signals a word that sounds the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Here means present, as when answering a register: 'Here!'

clue.text: Kind of friend to include love in the mix

indicators.note: the friend word takes in the love letter

parts.note: an ally is a kind of friend
love is zero in tennis, written O

explanation.surface: A sort of friend puts romance into the equation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to include' puts O inside ALLY.
explanation.definitionFit: An alloy is a metal made by mixing two or more metals.

clue.text: Vote for right in 2020?

parts.note: yea is a vote in favour

explanation.surface: A vote in favour of the right wing in the 2020 election.
explanation.walkthrough: '2020' looks like an election date, but it is an example of a year, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: 2020 is one particular year, so the definition is an example.

clue.text: Bob perhaps missing launch with part in theatre work

indicators.note: a word's launch is its start, so the first letter is lost

parts.note: Bob Hope was a famous American comedian, so Bob points to his surname
a ration is a portion, a part

explanation.surface: Bob tries his first role in a stage production.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing launch' cuts HOPE to OPE. 'theatre work' means surgery in an operating theatre, not a stage show.
explanation.definitionFit: Surgery is done in an operating theatre, so an operation is the work done there.

clue.text: Resident of Middle-earth not yielding collection of trees

parts.note: orcs are creatures living in Tolkien's Middle-earth
something hard does not yield to pressure

explanation.surface: A stubborn orc from Tolkien's world guards a group of trees.
explanation.definitionFit: An orchard is a planted group of fruit trees.

clue.text: Peak volume in middle of week then quiet

indicators.note: the volume letter goes inside the middle letters
the middle of a word is its central letters

parts.note: rest means quiet, as in peace and quiet

explanation.surface: Noise peaks midweek, and then things go quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'middle of week' gives EE; 'in' places the volume letter between those two Es.
explanation.definitionFit: Everest is the highest mountain on Earth, a peak.
